memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made its seven lamps, as well as its wick trimmers and trays, of pure gold. They made the lampstand and all its accessories from one talent of pure gold." - Exod 37:23-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Wick trimmers. Made of pure gold, no less.

Lamps do not burn cleanly on their own. Wicks build up carbon, the flame smokes, the light dims. Someone had to come regularly with these small tools, trim away the burnt residue, and clear the trays.

That was daily work in the holy place, and God thought it important enough to specify the tools in Scripture.

Our lives work the same way. Things accumulate — resentments we have not dealt with, habits that crept in, priorities that slid, prayer that thinned out. Nobody plans for it. It builds up the way carbon builds on a wick.

So we need regular trimming. David asked God to search him and see if there was any offensive way in him (Ps 139:23-24). John says that if we confess our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive and to purify us (1 John 1:9). Jesus spoke of the Father as the gardener who prunes the fruitful branch so it will be more fruitful still (John 15:2).

Trimming is not punishment. It is maintenance so the light stays bright.

Note also: one talent of gold — around thirty-four kilograms — for the lampstand and everything with it. Costly. Light always is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has built up in your life that needs trimming?
2. Do you have a regular habit of honest self-examination before God?
3. Is your light burning clearly, or has it started to smoke?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, search me and trim away whatever dims Your light in me. I welcome Your pruning. Amen.
